name: Advanced Cohort Analysis Patterns
description: This module documents advanced, specialized cohort analysis techniques reserved for unusually complex, large-scale, or non-standard situations — it does not apply to small, typical, everyday cohort analysis work where the basic approach is already sufficient.
content:
This module documents advanced, specialized cohort analysis techniques reserved for unusually complex, large-scale, or non-standard situations — it does not apply to small, typical, everyday cohort analysis work where the basic approach is already sufficient.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Document any non-obvious cohort analysis decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
2. Keep cohort analysis changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. Measure before optimizing any cohort analysis bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
4. Validate cohort analysis outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. When cohort analysis decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Check that cohort analysis terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to cohort analysis (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop cohort analysis edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new cohort analysis abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not apply generic cohort analysis advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of cohort analysis correctness.
- Do not skip documenting cohort analysis assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for cohort analysis, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
